items.title: Product search and filtering
items.body: Shoppers can only browse the full product list today, so finding a specific book means scrolling. Add search by title and author, filtering by price range, and sorting by price or title, with paged results. Use Postgres full-text search with a generated tsvector column and a GIN index rather than LIKE scans. An empty search returns the full catalogue. The migration that adds the index must run cleanly against a database that already has products in it. All work stays inside the catalog module.

items.title: Categories with browse-by-category
items.body: Products have no grouping, so there is no way to browse a subject area. Add a category entity in the catalog schema with a many-to-many link to products, category navigation in the site header rendered from the database, and a paged category listing page. A product can belong to more than one category. Include seed data for at least three categories. All work stays inside the catalog module.

items.title: Authors as first-class entities
items.body: The author is stored as a plain string on the product, so there is no way to list everything by one author. Replace it with an author entity and add an author page listing that author's books. Migrate existing author strings into the new table without losing data, then drop the old column in a separate migration so the two steps can be reviewed independently. The product page links to the author page. All work stays inside the catalog module.

items.title: Product images
items.body: Product pages have no imagery. Support multiple images per product with one designated as primary, served by the application, and shown as an ordered gallery on the detail page. The listing page uses the primary image. A product with no images falls back to a placeholder. Image ordering is stable across requests. The tech spec must decide where the image bytes live before implementation starts. All work stays inside the catalog module.
